culture.title: Klimt's The Kiss at the Upper Belvedere
culture.description: The gold-leaf painting everyone has seen reproduced, hanging in a baroque palace room where you finally see how much of it is actual metal.
culture.bonus: Look at it for a full two minutes before taking any photo.

culture.title: Morning Exercise at the Spanish Riding School
culture.description: For a fraction of the price of a gala you sit in the baroque Winter Riding School and watch the Lipizzaners do their actual daily training to classical music.
culture.bonus: Stay for a full hour rather than ducking out after ten minutes.

culture.title: The Beethoven Frieze at the Secession
culture.description: Klimt painted a thirty-four-metre frieze on three walls of a basement for a single 1902 exhibition, and it never left — still under the gold cabbage dome on Friedrichstrasse.
culture.bonus: Follow it left to right in order, the way it was meant to be read.

culture.title: The Bruegel Room at the Kunsthistorisches
culture.description: The Habsburgs' own collection, including the largest gathering of Bruegel panels anywhere — the Hunters in the Snow and the Tower of Babel in one room.
culture.bonus: Find five things happening in the background of the Hunters in the Snow.

culture.title: The State Rooms at Schönbrunn
culture.description: 1,441 rooms of Habsburg summer palace, of which you walk perhaps forty — including the hall of mirrors where a six-year-old Mozart performed for the empress.
culture.bonus: Work out which room you would actually want to live in.

culture.title: Composers' Graves at the Zentralfriedhof
culture.description: A cemetery bigger than the First District, where Beethoven, Schubert, Brahms and both Strausses are buried in one semicircle, around a monument to a Mozart nobody can find.
culture.bonus: Take tram 71 the whole way out, as the Viennese idiom for dying requires.

culture.title: Schiele at the Leopold Museum
culture.description: The largest Egon Schiele collection in the world, assembled by one obsessive ophthalmologist over fifty years, in a white limestone box in the MuseumsQuartier.
culture.bonus: Find the self-portrait that unsettles you most and work out why.

culture.title: Standing Room at the Vienna State Opera
culture.description: One of the great opera houses in the world sells a few hundred standing places for a handful of euros on the day — you queue, you get a rail, you tie a scarf to it to claim your spot.
culture.bonus: Queue for the standing places rather than buying a seat, and do the scarf properly.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Ring Tram Roulette
8ball.description: Get on tram 1 or 2 at any point on the Ringstrasse, ride until someone in the group says stop, and spend the rest of the evening within three blocks of wherever the doors open.
8ball.bonus: Eat and drink only at places you can see from where you got off.

8ball.title: Wildcard: Three Coffee Houses, One Afternoon
8ball.description: One melange in three different historic coffee houses in a single afternoon — a newspaper on a wooden rod at each, and no phone on the table at any of them.
8ball.bonus: Read one article properly in each and report back on all three.

social.title: Stelze and a Krug at the Schweizerhaus
social.description: A Prater beer garden since 1920, seating two thousand under the chestnut trees, serving roast pork knuckle and Budweiser Budvar poured straight from wooden casks.
social.bonus: Order one Stelze for the table and carve it yourselves.

social.title: Live Jazz at Porgy & Bess
social.description: A converted porn cinema turned into central Europe's most respected jazz room, programming something almost every night since 1993.
social.bonus: Buy a ticket for a name you have never heard of.

social.title: Glühwein at the Rathausplatz Christmas Market
social.description: The biggest of Vienna's Christmas markets, in front of a floodlit neo-Gothic City Hall, with a park behind it strung with lights and a heart-shaped tree.
social.bonus: Keep the mug deposit and take the mug home.

social.title: Brewery Tour at Ottakringer
social.description: Vienna's oldest and largest private brewery, brewing on the same site since 1837 — ninety minutes from brewhouse to bottling line, ending in eight fresh taps.
social.bonus: Pick your favourite of the eight before they tell you which is the flagship.

social.title: Late Night at Volksgarten Clubdiskothek
social.description: A club inside an imperial park pavilion, with a garden terrace that turns into a dance floor under the trees when the weather holds.
social.bonus: Dance outside in the garden rather than in the main room.

social.title: Ball Season at the Hofburg
social.description: For six weeks after New Year the city throws hundreds of formal balls — black tie, a live orchestra, a midnight quadrille, and dancing in imperial state rooms until dawn.
social.bonus: Learn enough of the left-turning waltz beforehand to survive the opening.

social.title: Deckchairs at Strandbar Herrmann
social.description: Imported sand, hundreds of deckchairs and a DJ on the bank of the Danube Canal, with the whole city apparently off work from two in the afternoon.
social.bonus: Claim a front-row deckchair before the after-work crowd lands.

social.title: The Bermuda Triangle Bar Crawl
social.description: A few dense blocks behind Schwedenplatz nicknamed for how reliably people disappear into them for a whole night — pubs, cellars and cocktail rooms, all walkable.
social.bonus: Let the group pick the next bar by whichever door is closest.

social.title: Drum and Bass at Flex
social.description: A club built into a disused metro tunnel on the Danube Canal with a sound system people travel for, and a terrace on the water when you need air.
social.bonus: Stay for the last hour of the set rather than leaving on a high.

social.title: Techno at Grelle Forelle
social.description: Vienna's most serious electronic room, under a bridge on the canal since 2011, with a strict no-photos policy and bookings that hold their own against Berlin.
social.bonus: Put the phone away for the entire night, as the room expects.

social.title: Cocktails at the Loos American Bar
social.description: Twenty-seven square metres of marble, mahogany and mirrors that Adolf Loos built in 1908 — the smallest bar in Vienna and one of the most important rooms in modern architecture.
social.bonus: Work out where the mirrors stop and the room actually ends.

social.title: Rooftop Drinks at Das LOFT
social.description: Eighteen floors up with a 360-degree wall of glass and a wildly coloured backlit ceiling by Pipilotti Rist, looking straight across at St Stephen's spire.
social.bonus: Get there before sunset and stay until the ceiling is the brightest thing in the room.

chill.title: Aperitivo on Franziskanerplatz at Kleines Café
chill.description: A cafe of about four tables on a cobbled square, designed by Hermann Czech, and the one Julie Delpy and Ethan Hawke sit outside in Before Sunrise.
chill.bonus: Take an outside table on the square and stay past dark.

chill.title: Roses in the Volksgarten
chill.description: Three thousand rose bushes laid out around a copy of a Greek temple, built on the rubble of fortifications Napoleon blew up.
chill.bonus: Find the most fragrant variety in the garden and learn its name.

chill.title: Enzis in the MuseumsQuartier Courtyard
chill.description: Big moulded loungers scattered across a baroque courtyard between the museums, recoloured every season, free to sprawl on for as long as you like.
chill.bonus: Stay on the same Enzi from daylight into dark.

chill.title: An Afternoon in the Stadtpark
chill.description: The city's first public park, with a river running through it, an art nouveau portal along one edge, and a gilded Johann Strauss playing violin to the lawn.
chill.bonus: Find a bench where you can see the gold Strauss and read a whole chapter.

chill.title: Street Art Along the Donaukanal
chill.description: Kilometres of legal wall running through the middle of the city, repainted constantly, so the same stretch is a different gallery every few weeks.
chill.bonus: Photograph one piece, then come back a month later and see what replaced it.

chill.title: The Palmenhaus at Schönbrunn
chill.description: A 110-metre iron-and-glass greenhouse from 1882 holding three climate zones, from Mediterranean scrub to full rainforest, in a single walk.
chill.bonus: Stay in the tropical wing until your glasses fog up completely.

chill.title: Laps at the Amalienbad
chill.description: A 1920s workers' bathhouse in Favoriten with a glass roof, gold mosaic and art deco tiling — arguably the most beautiful place to swim a length in Europe.
chill.bonus: Float on your back and just look at the ceiling for a while.

chill.title: The Butterfly House in the Burggarten
chill.description: An art nouveau palm house behind the Hofburg, half of it a humid greenhouse with free-flying tropical butterflies and half of it a very good brasserie.
chill.bonus: Stand still until one lands on you.

chill.title: Thermal Afternoon at Therme Wien
chill.description: Sulphur springs on the city's southern edge turned into one of Europe's largest urban spas — indoor and outdoor thermal pools plus a serious sauna world upstairs.
chill.bonus: Sit through one full Aufguss without leaving the sauna early.

chill.title: Hundertwasserhaus and Kunst Haus Wien
chill.description: A social housing block with no straight lines, uneven floors and trees growing out of the windows — then the museum round the corner explaining why.
chill.bonus: Find the trees that are registered as tenants.

foodie.title: Apfelstrudel at Café Landtmann
foodie.description: Freud's coffee house, on the Ring opposite the City Hall, where the strudel is pulled by hand and the terrace watches the whole city go past.
foodie.bonus: Sit on the terrace and order a second coffee you don't need.

foodie.title: Canal-Side Breakfast at Motto am Fluss
foodie.description: A 1950s ocean-liner interior built into the boat terminal at Schwedenplatz, with a top-deck terrace looking straight down the Danube Canal.
foodie.bonus: Take the top-deck terrace, whatever the queue for it.

foodie.title: Heuriger Evening at Mayer am Pfarrplatz
foodie.description: A wine tavern trading since 1683, in the house where Beethoven lived while going deaf — young wine by the quarter litre and food sold by weight at a buffet.
foodie.bonus: Drink the Gemischter Satz and nothing else all evening.

foodie.title: Graze the Naschmarkt
foodie.description: A kilometre and a half of stalls running down a covered-over river — Austrian cheese at one end, Levantine mezze at the other, and a new indoor hall as of 2026.
foodie.bonus: Eat something you can't name from three different stalls.

foodie.title: Three Michelin Stars at Steirereck
foodie.description: A mirrored pavilion in the Stadtpark holding Austria's most decorated kitchen, where Heinz Reitbauer builds entire courses around a single regional vegetable.
foodie.bonus: Let them choose the whole menu and the pairings, sight unseen.

foodie.title: Melange and a Newspaper at Café Hawelka
foodie.description: Smoke-darkened walls, art the owners took in lieu of payment, and a family still running the place their grandparents opened in 1939.
foodie.bonus: Stay long enough on one coffee that a waiter gives you a look.

foodie.title: The Original Sachertorte at Café Sacher
foodie.description: The cake at the centre of a seven-year Austrian lawsuit, eaten in the red-velvet room behind the opera house where the recipe has never left the building.
foodie.bonus: Eat it with unsweetened whipped cream, the way it's meant to be served.

foodie.title: Käsekrainer at Bitzinger
foodie.description: A sausage stand behind the opera house that has been serving cheese-filled Krainer to tuxedos and taxi drivers in the same queue since 1999.
foodie.bonus: Order in German, eat standing at the ledge, no plate.

foodie.title: The Schnitzel at Figlmüller
foodie.description: Since 1905, a schnitzel hammered so thin it overhangs the plate on every side — the version every other Viennese schnitzel gets measured against.
foodie.bonus: Finish it without asking for a box.

foodie.title: Open Sandwiches at Zum Schwarzen Kameel
foodie.description: A deli counter trading since 1618, where you stand at the bar with a glass of Grüner and eat tiny open sandwiches until you lose count of them.
foodie.bonus: Stand at the bar rather than sit, and order by pointing.

foodie.title: Tafelspitz at Plachutta
foodie.description: Boiled beef arrives at the table in its own copper pot of broth, and a waiter talks you through eating it in three courses, in the right order.
foodie.bonus: Do the marrow bone on toast properly, with salt, before anything else.

adventure.title: Twin City Liner to Bratislava
adventure.description: A catamaran leaves the Danube Canal in the middle of Vienna and has you in another country's old town in about seventy-five minutes.
adventure.bonus: Be back on Viennese soil by midnight.

adventure.title: Skate the Wiener Eistraum
adventure.description: Every winter the square in front of the City Hall becomes nine thousand square metres of ice, including winding skate paths that run off through the park trees.
adventure.bonus: Skate the whole winding path without touching the rail.

adventure.title: Climb to the Gloriette at Schönbrunn
adventure.description: Walk up the long meadow behind the palace to the colonnade Maria Theresa put on the hill, and look back down the axis at the whole baroque plan.
adventure.bonus: Get up there for sunrise, before the coach parties arrive.

adventure.title: Cycle the Wachau: Krems to Melk
adventure.description: An hour's train out of Vienna puts you on a flat riverside path through a UNESCO wine valley, past apricot orchards and ruined castles, ending at a baroque abbey on a cliff.
adventure.bonus: Stop at a roadside Heuriger and drink a Grüner Veltliner from the slope above you.

adventure.title: Climb at Kletterhalle Wien
adventure.description: Austria's largest climbing hall — sixteen metres tall, 2,300 square metres of wall, plus a whole floor of bouldering and a cafe bar to collapse into afterwards.
adventure.bonus: Finish a route that looked impossible when you walked in.

adventure.title: Boat on the Underground Lake at the Seegrotte
adventure.description: A flooded gypsum mine twenty minutes south of the city holds the largest underground lake in Europe, and you cross it by boat at a constant nine degrees.
adventure.bonus: Trail a hand in the water and keep it there for ten seconds.

adventure.title: Summer Day at Copa Beach
adventure.description: Vienna's improbable river beach at the head of the Danube Island — sand, swimming ladders straight into the channel, and a strip of bars behind it.
adventure.bonus: Swim across to the island side and walk back over the bridge.

adventure.title: Top of the Donauturm
adventure.description: Austria's highest viewpoint at 150 metres, a revolving restaurant above it, and Europe's highest slide spiralling 165 metres back down the outside.
adventure.bonus: Take the slide down instead of the lift.

adventure.title: Cycle the Donauinsel End to End
adventure.description: Twenty-one kilometres of car-free artificial island down the middle of the Danube, with swimming spots and bars strung along its whole length.
adventure.bonus: Stop and swim at least once before you reach the far end.

adventure.title: Wild Boar Walk in the Lainzer Tiergarten
adventure.description: A walled imperial hunting ground on the city's edge, still full of free-roaming wild boar and deer that will walk straight past you on the path.
adventure.bonus: Keep walking until a boar crosses the trail in front of you.

adventure.title: Swim and Row on the Alte Donau
adventure.description: A cut-off oxbow of the old Danube that Vienna turned into a lake — rent a wooden rowing boat by the hour and swim off the side of it.
adventure.bonus: Row far enough out that you can't hear the shore.

adventure.title: Paddleboard the Neue Donau
adventure.description: A flood-relief channel with no current and no boat traffic, which makes it the calmest water in the city and the easiest place in Vienna to stand on a board.
adventure.bonus: Paddle under at least three bridges before you turn around.

adventure.title: Ride the Wiener Riesenrad
adventure.description: The oldest Ferris wheel still turning anywhere in the world, built in 1897, with wooden cabins big enough to stand in and a Third Man scene shot from one of them.
adventure.bonus: Work out which cabin Orson Welles gave the cuckoo-clock speech from.

adventure.title: Run the Prater Hauptallee
adventure.description: Four and a half kilometres of dead-straight chestnut avenue laid out for Habsburg carriages, now the city's default running route from dawn onward.
adventure.bonus: Run the full length without stopping, then earn a beer at the far end.

adventure.title: Swim at the Krapfenwaldlbad
adventure.description: Vienna's highest outdoor pool, cut into pine forest on the Kahlenberg slope, where the whole city lies below the far end of the lane.
adventure.bonus: Swim a length looking only at the view, not the lane rope.

adventure.title: Stadtwanderweg 1: Kahlenberg to Leopoldsberg
adventure.description: A waymarked city trail through vineyards and the edge of the Vienna Woods to the two hills the city looks up at, then down into a wine village.
adventure.bonus: Finish at a Heuriger and drink the wine made on the slope you just walked.
